item.description:
Tidier menus, and a Clean Up that shows what it cleans

Wortel 2026.41.3 · 2026-10-06

Clean Up Worktrees, readable. In 2026.41.2 the list in Session ▸ Worktree ▸ Clean Up Worktrees… could collapse to nothing, leaving only the button. It now shows every worktree Wortel made, grouped by repository, one line each: tick what should go, see at a glance what’s clean and what’s kept, with “17 changes” or “In use” on the ones that stay. Rest the pointer on a row for the details, or right-click it to show it in Finder. One switch decides whether the branches Wortel made go too, and only ever the ones with nothing to lose.

Menus that read like a Mac app’s.

  • A new Tab menu holds everything about tabs: new terminal and browser tabs, moving between and moving tabs, reopening, and Close Tab.
  • The Session menu is down to what it’s about: starting sessions and folders, moving between sessions, the selected session’s own commands, and closing it. ⌘1 to ⌘9 still switch sessions, without nine rows for them.
  • The worktree commands sit together under Session ▸ Worktree.
  • Move To is greyed out when there’s nowhere to move the session.
  • View is in the order of the window: the sidebar and panels, the source control panes, the browser, then text size.
  • Show Sidebar and Hide Sidebar say which one they’ll do, Find has its own submenu, and the Wortel menu has Services and Show All, as every Mac app does.

Every keyboard shortcut works as before.

Also in this release: the usage-data note under the ⓘ in the sidebar could stay on screen and not go away when it first appeared while Wortel wasn’t the app you were in. It now closes when you switch to another app, and only appears once you’re back in Wortel.

Lighter in the background, and nothing left behind

Wortel 2026.41.2 · 2026-10-06

Much less work in the background. The source control panel used to re-read every repository it had ever shown each time a file changed, and to count the changes in every worktree on almost every switch. On a big repository with agents busy in a few worktrees, that could keep several cores busy and the fan spinning. Now only the repository you’re looking at is read. The others note that something changed and catch up when you come back to them, with a small spinner while they do. The Files pane does no work while it’s hidden.

Switching sessions is lighter. Moving between two sessions whose side columns differ no longer resizes every terminal in the app, which made every agent redraw its whole screen. A terminal takes its size when you show it.

Worktrees are cleaned up, safely. Closing a session in a worktree now says what’s in it and what will happen to it, and Session ▸ Clean Up Worktrees… lists every worktree Wortel made. One with nothing unsaved is removed, folder and branch. One with commits that exist nowhere else keeps its branch unless you tick it. One with uncommitted changes, or something running in it, is kept, and Wortel says why. Folders go to the Trash, so nothing is gone for good.

Nothing left running.

  • When your git settings turn on its file watcher, Wortel no longer starts one for every repository it looks at. They never exited, and piled up.
  • Closing a session you hadn’t opened since launch now ends its shell, instead of leaving it, and any agent in it, running out of sight.
  • A shell Wortel lost track of comes back at launch as a Recovered session if something is running in it, and is closed if it’s idle.
  • A fetch, pull or push that hangs is stopped after five minutes, and anything git started stops with it when you quit.

ssh sets up once. Connecting to a host installs its terminfo the first time only, instead of printing “Setting up xterm-ghostty terminfo” and leaving a folder in /tmp on every connection.

Also in this release:

  • Pasted images are cleared from the temp folder after a day.
  • If the list of sessions can’t be read, it’s set aside instead of being overwritten.

Window tiling is back, and the browser keeps its size

Wortel 2026.41.1 · 2026-10-05

Window tiling is back. Since the new titlebar, Fill, Center and everything under Window ▸ Move & Resize were greyed out, and their shortcuts (fn-⌃C to center, fn-⌃F to fill, fn-⌃ and an arrow for a half) did nothing. They work again. Dragging a tab in the titlebar still moves the tab, not the window.

The browser keeps its size. A browser in the side column could come back at its narrowest after you switched to another session and back. And once you had hidden and shown the sidebar, switching the column between the browser and Files or Changes could make it jump in width. Both are fixed: the column stays the width you gave it. If a session’s browser already got stuck narrow, drag it wide once and it stays.
